policy_title: Evict foreign nationals from social housing (three-month rule)
stated: Reform UK would require non-UK citizens living in social (council) housing to leave it for private rented accommodation within three months; those who fail to do so would lose their right to remain in the UK and face deportation. Social housing would be prioritised for military veterans and long-term local residents, with the most vulnerable exempt from the stricter rules. Announced by party leader Nigel Farage in June 2026 (his first Substack essay), ahead of the Makerfield by-election.

source.quote: Non-UK citizens who fail to leave social housing after a three-month grace period would lose their right to remain in Britain; social housing would be prioritised for veterans and long-term local residents, with the most vulnerable exempt.

bearing_set.reason: The policy directly reallocates social housing stock by removing all non-UK citizens from it, materially changing who can access social/affordable tenure and on what terms — a primary effect on the affordable housing fundamental.

The policy deploys loss of the right to remain and deportation as a sanction for occupying social housing, raising due-process and proportionality concerns, and makes a nationality-based distinction in the allocation of a public entitlement — directly engaging equal-treatment and legal-rights-framework questions within O9's strict scope.

Using loss of the right to remain (deportation) as the enforcement mechanism for a housing-compliance rule is a significant coercive state power directed at residents' lives and homes; this directly bears on freedom from state coercion indicators.

A policy that gives existing residents of a defined national group a three-month ultimatum to vacate their homes under threat of expulsion has a plausible, concrete mechanism for worsening inter-group trust, sense of belonging, and community integration for affected groups and their wider networks.

membership_note: Four fundamentals bear genuinely: O1 (social housing reallocation and private-rental knock-on), O9 (differential treatment by nationality with deportation sanction), O10 (deportation as coercive enforcement of a housing rule), and O15 (targeted expulsion threat's effect on belonging and inter-group trust). Public-finance effects are too uncertain in net (enforcement costs vs. subsidy savings) to clear the non-negligible bar for O12.
